name: jobs
description: Inspect, await and control existing work, regardless of the adapter or agent that performs it.

content.inline:
## Jobs
A Job is the universal handle for one operation invocation. It is not owned by the Grid adapter. Keep the exact ID and the venue that hosts it.
- Use Job-status with {id, venue?, authenticateAs?} to read status, progress, output/error and remote observations.
- Use Job-result with {id, timeout?, venue?, authenticateAs?} for the exact output. A positive timeout bounds only your wait; 0 or omission waits indefinitely. Failure or cancellation of a wait never cancels the target. Do not resubmit work because a wait timed out.
- Use Job-cancel to request cancellation. Completed outcomes stay unchanged; cancellation does not undo side effects or prove that remote work stopped. Read delegation observations when present.
- Use Job-message with {id, message: {content: "..."}, venue?, authenticateAs?} to answer a Job that needs input. The message uses the receiving operation's format. Accepted delivery is not completion.
- Pause/resume are optional controls and refuse when the execution adapter cannot support them. INPUT_REQUIRED and AUTH_REQUIRED usually need a message, not resume.
- Omit venue for a local Job, including a local proxy. To address a destination Job directly, use its own ID and venue. Explicit remote authentication follows the Grid connection policy; caller needs a credential for that target, and venue mode is only for the venue itself.
- Select tools from the advertised palette. These operations inspect/control existing work; submission belongs to the operation or agent you want to invoke.
